newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan overnight rates firm at 9.50 pct, tight mkt.
newsitem.headline: Jordan overnight rates firm at 9.50 pct, tight mkt.

text.p: Overnight rates on the Jordanian dinar stood at 9.50 compared with a 9.00-9.50 range on Monday in a squeezed market, dealers said.
"The market continues to be very tight," said one dealer. "It looks like there is an agreement among banks to stay at 9.50 to avoid a re-purchasing of certificates of deposit CDs."
The Central Bank of Jordan said on Sunday it was offering banks 15 million dinars in CDs in this week's auction.
Interest yields released on Sunday from last week's auction were unchanged at 9.250 percent for three-month papers and 9.500 percent for six-months.
Overnight rates on the dinar rose again on Thursday to 8.50-9.50 percent from Wednesday's 8.00 to 9.00 percent after the Central Bank pulled more funds out of the market.
Rates soared on Wednesday from the 3.00 percent to 5.00 percent range, where they had been stuck for over a week.

Bankers said the Central Bank might be keen to hoist overnight rates to give banks incentive to hunt for longer-term deposits from clients, increasing the amount of dinar-held accounts and resisting any slip towards dollarisation.
With overnight rates so low, banks had little motive to borrow money long-term at higher rates, they said.
